hero.title: Kubar Labs
hero.subtitle: Building the origination layer between fragmented B2B platforms and lenders
hero.intro: Kubar Labs builds NavDhan, embedded origination infrastructure that converts borrower intent and permissioned platform signals into lender-ready applications for existing lender systems.

mission_vision.mission_text: Make business credit easier to originate by embedding lender-ready workflows inside the platforms businesses already use.
mission_vision.vision_text: A business-credit ecosystem where viable enterprises can be understood through their operating context and connected to suitable regulated lenders.

why_we_exist.title: Why we exist
why_we_exist.p1: Business-lending infrastructure has improved, but origination across fragmented B2B ecosystems remains difficult to scale.
why_we_exist.p2: Millions of small businesses transact through marketplaces, procurement systems, ERPs and sector-specific platforms, yet financing is often disconnected from those workflows and the operating context they contain.
why_we_exist.p3: Our research with businesses, platforms and lenders showed that the bottleneck is not only capital. It is the ability to capture intent, structure permissioned data and deliver lender-ready applications efficiently.
why_we_exist.p4: We started Kubar Labs to build that origination layer.

how_we_work.title: How we work
how_we_work.subtitle: We build origination infrastructure around three principles:

1.title: Platform-Specific Intelligence
1.desc: Generic applications miss the operating context available inside business platforms. NavDhan structures permissioned signals such as transaction patterns, inventory cycles, payment behaviour and sector-specific operating data for lender-configured pre-qualification.

2.title: Embedded Origination
2.desc: Credit requests begin inside B2B platforms, marketplaces, ERPs and enterprise workflows. NavDhan captures intent at the point of need and creates lender-ready applications without becoming a separate borrower-destination marketplace.

3.title: Pre-Disbursement Orchestration
3.desc: NavDhan coordinates application collection, data verification, pre-qualification and routing into existing lender systems. The regulated lender retains underwriting, pricing, approval, documentation, disbursal and servicing.

1.label: Horizon 1
1.title: NavDhan
1.desc: NavDhan embeds inside fragmented B2B platforms, captures borrower intent and permissioned operational signals, and routes lender-ready applications into existing lender systems. Lenders pay transaction, origination and later recurring platform fees. Final credit decisions remain with regulated lenders.

2.label: Horizon 2
2.title: Kubar Protocol
2.desc: Kubar Protocol is longer-term R&D focused on digital trade assets and cross-border settlement infrastructure. Nearer-term eBL and LC financing remain use cases of NavDhan's origination layer.

traction.desc: We have developed NavDhan through incubation programmes, grants, technical credits, product co-design and commercial discussions. Relationship labels below must distinguish recognitions, design partners, active integration discussions, pilot interest and ecosystem programmes.

partnerships.2: betterfinance and Interestng — Phase 1 lending partners.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.p1: Lenders have scaled decisioning and servicing infrastructure, but origination across fragmented B2B ecosystems remains manual and intermediary-led.
roadmap.p2: Phase 1 launches managed origination for unsecured business loans, allowing NavDhan to validate application quality, lender matching, operating costs and repayment-linked economics.
roadmap.p3: Phase 2 scales the Embedded Credit SDK across platform and lender integrations, adds recurring infrastructure revenue and supports secured business-credit use cases.
roadmap.p4: Phase 3 extends the origination layer into eBL and LC financing, while Kubar Protocol remains a separate longer-term R&D initiative for digital trade assets and cross-border settlement.

hero.diagram_eyebrow: FROM TRADE EVIDENCE TO AN ACCEPTED RECEIVABLE
hero.transition_note: Issuing-bank acceptance is the decisive transition.
hero.qualification: Banks, lenders and external document providers retain their authority. This is an illustrative workflow, not a live transaction.

progress.title:
A demonstrated prototype.
A product in development.
progress.description: We demonstrated the lifecycle with synthetic trade data and simulated institutional adapters. No external money moved and no live partner, bank, venue or regulator system was contacted.
progress.note: Development status: August 2026. Demonstration does not imply production availability.
progress.demonstrated_description: Synthetic adapters connected order and LC context, document evidence, simulated bank acceptance, financing and simulated settlement.
progress.development_description: Work continues on institution-facing integrations, permissioned access and operating controls. Availability remains subject to institutional readiness and applicable requirements.

workflow.title:
Follow the trade.
Keep the authority clear.
workflow.description: An example lifecycle for LC-backed export finance. Availability depends on the institutions, approvals and regulated venues involved.

1.title: Begin with the trade commitment.
1.description: Connect the order, counterparties and letter-of-credit context into a permissioned trade record.

2.title: Connect pre-shipment finance.
2.description: A bank may provide packing credit in foreign currency (PCFC), subject to its assessment and requirements.

3.title: Link shipment evidence.
3.description: Bring shipment events and external electronic bill-of-lading references into the record without assuming control of those documents.

4.title: Identify the accepted receivable.
4.description: Documentary evidence alone is not an accepted receivable. Authoritative issuing-bank acceptance establishes the Accepted LC Receivable.

5.title: Connect eligible financing.
5.description: Carry the accepted receivable and its verified context into an eligible funding workflow through the relevant regulated venue.

6.title: Settle through the bank.
6.description: The bank executes the settlement waterfall: PCFC repayment and the exporter’s balance. Payment to the financier at maturity is a separate, later event.

authority.bank_summary: Credit approval and settlement stay with the relevant banks and regulated institutions. Kubar Protocol does not lend or hold financing proceeds.
authority.bank_detail: The bank executes the financing-proceeds waterfall: PCFC repayment and the exporter’s balance. The financier’s maturity payment is a separate, later event under the financing terms.
authority.evidence_summary: External document providers retain document control. An accepted receivable requires authoritative issuing-bank acceptance—not just uploaded documents.
authority.evidence_detail: Protocol links references and permissioned context. It is not the default controller of the electronic bill of lading, and does not replace the issuing bank or document provider’s authority.
authority.role_boundary: Kubar Protocol does not become the lender, custodian, regulated venue or settlement bank.
